acceptanceResults: Capture a reproducible identity-bound baseline and candidate for status warm startup, medium repository observation, and one Work Item verification route; report samples, median, filesRead/filesHashed, gitCalls, executed/reused nodes, workers, and elapsedMs without claiming provider or enterprise performance.

Reduce measured Rust Runtime cost through request-scoped reuse, bounded memoization, or equivalent Rust-native changes while preserving repository isolation, snapshot identity, Contract semantics, required gates, evidence binding, and fail-closed behavior; a Git snapshot must not re-enumerate the same source tree for its derived digest.

The performance fixture reaches the documented status <50 ms and observation <100 ms targets on the declared local platform, or records an explicit bounded gap and fails the performance gate rather than weakening governance; no unmeasured speedup claim is accepted.
Repeated requests for the same repository snapshot reuse only matching identity-bound observations/verification results; changed or unknown inputs execute the declared checks and record the reason.

Independent Work Items may execute in parallel only with disjoint repository scopes and receive separate Work Item evidence receipts; no cross-Work-Item receipt or global current-repository state is introduced.

Performance regression, repository isolation, lifecycle, and full workspace tests pass; tri-language performance documentation states the installation boundary as shared external Runtime plus explicit --repo and does not copy reference installers, Make/Python, SDK, or V1 runtime behavior.
Adopter-facing performance guidance and acceptance steps are reproducible with the published/installed Runtime and preserve per-repository Runtime and evidence identities.
